Description: explicit — route shields missing badge on the open OpenMapTiles stack
prompt: I'm using an open OpenMapTiles / OSM-based vector basemap with MapLibre GL JS (no Mapbox account). My interstate and US highway shields render as bare floating numbers with no shield badge behind them; the numbers are fine. My tiles do populate network, ref, and ref_length. Which exact sprite image names do the shield layers expect, and how do I get the badges to appear without editing the layers?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
### TL;DR  
The shield layers that come with the **OpenMapTiles / OSM‑Bright** style look for the following sprite IDs  

| Network (layer) | Sprite IDs (badge images) |
|-----------------|---------------------------|
| **US Interstate** | `us-interstate_1`, `us-interstate_2`, `us-interstate_3`, `us-interstate_4`, `us-interstate_5`, `us-interstate_6` |
| **US Highway**   | `us-highway_1`, `us-highway_2`, `us-highway_3`, `us-highway_4`, `us-highway_5`, `us-highway_6` |
| **US State**      | `us-state_1`, `us-state_2`, `us-state_3`, `us-state_4`, `us-state_5`, `us-state_6` |
| **Generic road** | `road_1`, `road_2`, `road_3`, `road_4`, `road_5`, `road_6` |

> **Why the numbers are still there** – the `text-field` expression (`{ref}`) draws the route number with the glyphs font. The badge behind it is an `icon-image` that must exist in the sprite sheet. If the sprite does not contain the ID that the layer asks for, MapLibre silently drops the icon, leaving only the number.

Below is a step‑by‑step recipe to make the badges appear **without touching any layer definitions**.

---

## 1. Verify which sprite the style is currently using

```json
{
  "sprite": "https://demotiles.maplibre.org/styles/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite"
}
```

If you have changed the `sprite` property to point at your own host, make sure the host actually contains **all** of the IDs listed above. A common mistake is to copy only the PNG file (or only the JSON) or to host a *minimal* sprite that omits the shield images.

---

## 2. Get a complete sprite that contains the shield images

### Option A – Use the official OSM‑Bright sprite (recommended)

The OSM‑Bright style ships a full sprite that already includes every shield badge:

```
https://demotiles.maplibre.org/styles/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite.json
https://demotiles.maplibre.org/styles/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite.png
```

*If you want to self‑host (to avoid third‑party rate limits, add your own CORS headers, etc.)*:

1. **Download the two files** (and the `@2x` versions if you need Hi‑DPI support):
   ```bash
   curl -O https://demotiles.maplibre.org/styles/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite.json
   curl -O https://demotiles.maplibre.org/styles/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite.png
   curl -O https://demotiles.maplibre.org/styles/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite@2x.json
   curl -O https://demotiles.maplibre.org/styles/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite@2x.png
   ```
2. **Upload the four files** to a static host you control (GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel, S3, Cloudflare Workers Sites, etc.).  
   The base URL will be something like `https://mydomain.com/sprites/osm-bright`.

3. **Point the style at the new base URL**:

   ```json
   {
     "sprite": "https://mydomain.com/sprites/osm-bright"
   }
   ```

   *Do not add the `.json` or `.png` extensions – MapLibre adds them automatically.*

### Option B – Add a *second* sprite sheet that only contains the shields

If you already have a custom sprite for your own POI icons and you don’t want to merge the two, you can use the **array form** introduced in MapLibre GL JS 3.0:

```json
{
  "sprite": [
    { "id": "default", "url": "https://mydomain.com/sprites/my-poi" },
    { "id": "shields", "url": "https://mydomain.com/sprites/osm-bright" }
  ]
}
```

*Important:*  
* The shield layers in the OSM‑Bright style use the **default** sheet, i.e. they reference `icon-image: "us-interstate_{ref_length}"` (no prefix).  
* By giving the OSM‑Bright sheet the **id `"default"`** you keep the original layer expressions unchanged.  
* If you give it any other id (e.g. `"shields"`), you would have to edit every `icon-image` expression to add the prefix (`"shields:us-interstate_{ref_length}"`). Since the question asks for a solution *without editing layers*, keep the id `"default"`.

---

## 3. Make sure CORS and MIME types are correct

* **CORS** – The sprite JSON and PNG must be reachable from the page that loads the map. The simplest way is to serve them from the same origin as the style, or configure the host to send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (or your domain).  
* **MIME types** – Serve the JSON with `application/json` and the PNG with `image/png`. Most static hosts do this automatically.

If you see a 404 or a CORS error in the browser console when the map tries to fetch `…/sprite.json` or `…/sprite.png`, the badge will never appear.

---

## 4. Verify the sprite actually contains the needed IDs

Open the JSON file in a browser or with `jq` and grep for the IDs:

```bash
jq 'keys[]' sprite.json | grep '^us-interstate_'   # should list 1‑6
jq 'keys[]' sprite.json | grep '^us-highway_'      # should list 1‑6
jq 'keys[]' sprite.json | grep '^us-state_'        # should list 1‑6
jq 'keys[]' sprite.json | grep '^road_'            # should list 1‑6
```

If any of the expected keys are missing, the badge will not render for that length. The official OSM‑Bright sprite contains **all** of them.

---

## 5. (Optional) Fallback for *any* missing image – `setMissingStyleImageResolver`

If you cannot guarantee that the sprite will always have every badge (e.g. you are serving a very small custom sprite), you can supply a runtime resolver that draws a placeholder or fetches the missing image on‑the‑fly:

```js
map.setMissingStyleImageResolver((id) => {
  // id will be something like "us-interstate_3"
  // Return a Promise that resolves to an ImageBitmap or a Canvas
  return fetch(`https://mydomain.com/fallback-shields/${id}.png`)
    .then(r => r.blob())
    .then(b => createImageBitmap(b));
});
```

This **does not require any layer changes**, but it does require a small amount of JavaScript. In most cases simply using a complete sprite (steps 1‑4) is easier.

---

## 6. Quick checklist – after you change the sprite

| ✅ | Check |
|---|-------|
| **Sprite URL** points to a base URL (no extension) that serves `sprite.json` and `sprite.png` (and `@2x` if you need Hi‑DPI). |
| **Sprite JSON** contains `us-interstate_1 … us-interstate_6`, `us-highway_1 … us-highway_6`, `us-state_1 … us-state_6`, and `road_1 … road_6`. |
| **CORS** headers allow the map page to fetch the files. |
| **Network tab** shows HTTP 200 for `…/sprite.json` and `…/sprite.png`. |
| **Console** shows no “style image missing” warnings. |
| **Map** now shows shields with the badge behind the number. |

If all of the above are true, the shields will render correctly **without any modification to the style’s layers**.

---

## 7. Summary answer to the original question

*The shield layers expect the following sprite image IDs:*

```
us-interstate_1 … us-interstate_6
us-highway_1   … us-highway_6
us-state_1     … us-state_6
road_1         … road_6   (fallback for networks that don’t have a dedicated set)
```

*To make the badges appear without editing any layer definitions:*

1. Use a sprite sheet that contains **all** of those IDs (the official OSM‑Bright sprite does).  
2. Host that sprite yourself (or keep the original URL) and set the style’s `sprite` property to the base URL of that sheet.  
3. Ensure the sprite is served with correct CORS headers and MIME types.  

That’s it – the existing `icon-image` expressions (`"us-interstate_{ref_length}"`, `"us-highway_{ref_length}"`, etc.) will automatically resolve to the newly‑available badge images, and the shields will render with their proper background.

Description: implicit — own icon sheet alongside the basemap provider's, icons never appear
prompt: My MapLibre GL JS style's sprite points at my basemap provider's URL. I host my own sheet of POI icons on my own domain, and I set icon-image on my symbol layer to one of my icon names. The basemap's own icons all render fine, but mine never appear and nothing logs an error. I'd rather not merge the two sheets or rebuild them. How do I get my symbol layers to reference the icons in my sheet?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
## TL;DR  

1. **Turn the `sprite` property into an *array* of sprite sheets** (MapLibre GL JS ≥ 3.0).  
2. Give the basemap’s sheet the special id **`default`** (so all the existing `icon‑image` values keep working).  
3. Give your own sheet any other id, e.g. **`my‑icons`**.  
4. **Reference your icons with the prefix** `my‑icons:` – e.g. `"icon-image": "my-icons:cafe"` .  

That’s all you need – no merging, no rebuilding, no runtime `addImage()` calls.

Below is a complete walk‑through, plus a checklist of the most common gotchas that make the icons silently disappear.

---

## 1. Why the icons never appear

| Symptom | Typical cause |
|---------|----------------|
| Basemap icons render, your POI icons never show, **no error** in the console | The style is still looking for the icon in the *single* sprite sheet you gave it (`sprite: "https://provider.com/sprites/basemap"`). The name you wrote (`"cafe"`) is **not** in that sheet, so MapLibre silently drops the symbol. |
| You see a blank point (or a fallback “missing‑image” marker) only when you inspect the network tab | The request that fails is `https://provider.com/sprites/basemap/cafe.png` (or `cafe@2x.png`). Because the file does not exist, the request returns 404 and the layer is omitted. |
| No request for your own sprite at all | The style never knows about your sheet – you haven’t told MapLibre to load it. |

The fix is to **declare both sprite sheets** in the style file.

---

## 2. The array form of `sprite`

Since **MapLibre GL JS v3.0** the `sprite` root property can be either:

* a **string** (the classic single‑sheet form), **or**
* an **array of objects** `{ id, url }`.

```json
{
  "sprite": [
    { "id": "default", "url": "https://tiles.provider.com/sprites/basemap" },
    { "id": "my-icons", "url": "https://example.com/sprites/poi" }
  ]
}
```

### Rules that matter

| Rule | What it means for you |
|------|-----------------------|
| **`id: "default"`** is the *only* id that can be omitted when you reference an image. All other ids **must be prefixed**. | Keep the provider’s sheet as `default` so you don’t have to touch any of the existing `icon-image` values in the style. |
| **Reference syntax** → `"{id}:{image-name}"` | Your POI layer must use `"my-icons:cafe"` (or whatever the exact name is in the POI sprite JSON). |
| **All URLs are extension‑less** – MapLibre adds `.json`, `.png`, and `@2x` automatically. | Do **not** add `.json` or `.png` to the `url` field. |
| **All ids must be unique** – duplicate ids cause a validation error (`all the sprites' ids must be unique`). | Use a distinct id (`my-icons`, `extra`, `custom`, …). |
| **CORS** – the sprite PNG/JSON must be served with `Access‑Control‑Allow‑Origin: *` (or your origin). | If you host the POI sprite on a different domain, make sure the static host sends the proper CORS header, otherwise the browser will block the image silently. |

---

## 3. Step‑by‑step implementation

### 3.1. Prepare your POI sprite

1. **Generate the sprite** (PNG + JSON) from your SVG icons.  
   *Tools*: `spritezero`, `spreet`, or the Martin web UI.  
2. **Upload the two files** (and the optional `@2x` versions) to a location you control, e.g. `https://example.com/sprites/poi.png` and `https://example.com/sprites/poi.json`.  
3. **Check CORS** – a quick `curl -I` should show:

   ```bash
   curl -I https://example.com/sprites/poi.json
   # → HTTP/2 200
   # → access-control-allow-origin: *
   ```

   If you’re on S3, set the bucket policy to allow public reads; on Netlify/Vercel the default is fine.

### 3.2. Edit the style JSON

Open the style file (or the style editor you use) and replace the single `sprite` string with the array:

```json
{
  // … other root properties …
  "sprite": [
    {
      "id": "default",
      "url": "https://tiles.provider.com/sprites/basemap"
    },
    {
      "id": "my-icons",
      "url": "https://example.com/sprites/poi"
    }
  ],
  // … rest of the style …
}
```

> **Tip** – If you are using a style‑hosting service (MapTiler Cloud, Mapbox Studio, etc.) that only lets you set a single URL, you’ll need to host the *combined* style JSON yourself (or switch to a self‑hosted style). The array form is part of the **style spec**, not a proprietary extension, so any GL‑compatible loader will understand it.

### 3.3. Update your POI layer(s)

```json
{
  "id": "poi-cafes",
  "type": "symbol",
  "source": "my-poi-source",
  "source-layer": "poi",
  "layout": {
    "icon-image": "my-icons:cafe",          // <‑‑ note the prefix
    "icon-size": 0.8,
    "icon-allow-overlap": true
  },
  "paint": {
    "icon-color": "#006600"
  }
}
```

If you have many layers, you can use a variable in the style (e.g. a property expression) but the **prefix must be present**:

```json
"icon-image": ["concat", "my-icons:", ["get", "icon_name"]]
```

### 3.4. Verify in the browser

1. Open the page with your MapLibre map.  
2. Open DevTools → **Network** → filter `poi.json` / `poi.png`. You should see two requests:

   ```
   https://example.com/sprites/poi.json
   https://example.com/sprites/poi.png
   ```

   (and the `@2x` variants if you have a high‑DPI display).  
3. In the **Console** you should **not** see any `Style image missing` warnings.  
4. The POI points should now show the custom icons.

---

## 4. Common pitfalls & how to spot them

| Symptom | What to check |
|---------|----------------|
| **No network request for your sprite** | Did you forget to change the `sprite` property to an array? Did you accidentally leave a stray `sprite: "…" ` somewhere else (e.g. in a style‑layer `metadata`)? |
| **404 on `…/poi.json` or `…/poi.png`** | URL typo, missing file, or the server is refusing the request (CORS). Verify the exact URL in the browser address bar. |
| **CORS error in console** (`Cross‑origin request blocked`) | The sprite host must send `Access‑Control‑Allow‑Origin`. On S3 set `CORSConfiguration`; on Netlify add a `_headers` file with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. |
| **Icons still missing, but network shows 200** | The **image name** you use does not match any key in the sprite JSON. Open the JSON file and grep for the name (`cafe`). Remember that the JSON stores the *raw* name, **without** the prefix. |
| **Only the 1× PNG loads, the 2× version is missing** | If you have a high‑DPI screen, MapLibre will request `poi@2x.png`. Provide that file (or accept the 1× fallback). |
| **Using an older MapLibre version (< 3.0)** | The array form is not supported. Upgrade to at least `3.0.0`, or fall back to the classic approach: merge the sheets **or** load your icons at runtime with `map.loadImage()` + `map.addImage()`. |
| **`icon-image` is an expression that drops the prefix** | Expressions are evaluated per feature. If you build the name with `["get", "icon_name"]` you must prepend the prefix inside the expression: `["concat", "my-icons:", ["get", "icon_name"]]`. |

---

## 5. Alternative if you cannot upgrade to v3

If you are stuck on MapLibre GL JS v2 (or an older fork) you have two options:

1. **Merge the two sprite sheets** (use `spritezero` to combine PNG + JSON).  
2. **Load your POI icons at runtime**:

   ```js
   // Example using async/await
   async function addCustomIcons(map) {
     const icons = ['cafe', 'library', 'park']; // names of your SVG files
     for (const name of icons) {
       const url = `https://example.com/sprites/poi/${name}.svg`;
       const img = await map.loadImage(url);
       map.addImage(name, img, { sdf: false }); // set sdf:true if you need tinting
     }
   }

   const map = new maplibregl.Map({ /* … */ });
   map.on('style.load', () => addCustomIcons(map));
   ```

   This works fine for a handful of icons, but it **does not scale** (no stretchX/Y, no content box, no automatic @2x handling) and you lose the ability to reference them via the sprite JSON.

---

## 6. Bonus: Using `setMissingStyleImageResolver` (MapLibre v6)

If you are on **MapLibre v6** (the latest major version at the time of writing) you can also supply a *fallback* resolver that will be called whenever an `icon-image` cannot be found in any loaded sprite sheet:

```js
map.setMissingStyleImageResolver((id) => {
  // id will be something like "my-icons:cafe"
  const [sheetId, name] = id.split(':');
  if (sheetId === 'my-icons') {
    // fetch the image on‑the‑fly, return a Promise<ImageData>
    return fetch(`https://example.com/sprites/poi/${name}.png`)
      .then(r => r.blob())
      .then(blob => createImageBitmap(blob));
  }
  // return null to keep the default “missing image” behavior
  return null;
});
```

That approach lets you keep a **single** sprite URL (the provider’s) and lazily load missing icons from elsewhere. It’s handy for *very* dynamic icon sets, but for a static POI catalog the array‑form is still the cleanest solution.

---

## 7. Quick checklist before you ship

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| **MapLibre version ≥ 3.0** (or v6 with `setMissingStyleImageResolver`) |
| `sprite` is an **array** with two objects: `default` (provider) + `my-icons` (your sheet) |
| URLs are **extension‑less** (`…/sprites/poi` not `…/poi.json`) |
| Your POI sprite **JSON** contains the exact image names you use |
| All requests to `…/sprites/poi.*` return **200** and have **CORS** headers |
| `icon-image` on POI layers uses the **`my-icons:`** prefix (or an expression that adds it) |
| If you use `icon-text-fit` for shields, the sprite entry includes `stretchX/Y` and `content` (optional but recommended) |
| Tested on a **high‑DPI** screen (both `@1x` and `@2x` PNGs load) |
| No `styleimagemissing` warnings in the console after the map loads |

If you tick all the boxes, your custom POI icons will appear side‑by‑side with the basemap’s icons, without any merging or rebuilding of the original sprite sheet.
